transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Yeah, hi. Um… I guess I came in because things got a little out of hand with work stuff. I’m usually just one of the crew guys, you know, landscaping, groundskeeping, that kind of thing, but lately I kind of jumped into trying to run three bids at once, calling city people, lining up plant suppliers, messaging pretty much everybody I knew about this park idea I had.

I mean, it felt productive at first, like I was just being motivated, but… I couldn’t really shut it off. It was a lot. Does that make sense?
During this time, were you needing much less sleep than usual?

I’m not totally sure how to answer that. I mean… I wasn’t really tracking it. I probably wasn’t sleeping great, but I don’t know if I’d say I needed way less sleep, you know? I was just kind of staying busy and then realizing it was late. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
During this time, did you hear or see things that other people couldn’t?
No… I don’t think so. Not like hearing voices or seeing things, if that’s what you mean. I mean, I was really caught up in my own head, but I don’t think there was anything like that.
During that time, did you feel unusually high or euphoric?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t know if I’d call it euphoric exactly, but I definitely felt… fired up. Like more confident than usual, almost like the plan was bigger than me and I could just make it happen.

I’m not proud of this part, but if someone at work questioned it or told me to slow down, I’d get really irritated. I snapped at a coworker pretty hard over basically nothing. At the time it felt justified, but looking back, it was more intense than it needed to be. Does that count as what you mean?
During that time, did your behavior cause serious problems at work or in your life?

I mean… I wouldn’t say everything fell apart or anything. I’m still showing up, still trying to do a good job.

But yeah, it’s started causing problems. I’ve been missing details on bids and measurements, stuff I normally catch. And with the kind of work I do, one bad mistake can be a big deal. I keep thinking, like, if I measure wrong or overlook something, it could cost me clients… or worse, someone could get hurt on a job site.

So… yeah, I guess it’s more serious than I’d like to admit. Is that what you mean?
During that time, were you talking more than usual?

I’m not totally sure. I mean, I talk at work anyway, so it’s hard for me to tell what’s “more than usual.”

Maybe I was explaining myself more, or kind of going on when I thought people weren’t getting it… but I don’t know if it was enough that other people would notice. I don’t want to overstate it. Does that answer what you’re asking?
Did other people tell you that you were talking unusually fast or that they had trouble interrupting you?

No… not that anyone said to me directly. I don’t think anyone told me I was talking too fast or that they couldn’t get a word in.

Maybe I was a little more intense when I was explaining things, but I don’t remember anybody actually saying that. I could ask, I guess, if that would help?
At any point, did you have a strong belief that other people found unrealistic or clearly not true?

I mean… I don’t know if I’d call it “not true,” exactly, but looking back, maybe it was kind of unrealistic.

I honestly believed I was about to become, like, the guy every town around here would call for sustainable landscaping. Like I was right on the edge of something big. And… I mean, that sounds embarrassing saying it out loud, because I’m still just trying to keep my smaller jobs paid up and keep things steady.

At the time it felt believable, though. Like it made sense in my head. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
About how many days in a row did this fired-up, unusually confident period last?

Um… if I’m being honest, it was probably about two weeks in a row.

It kind of started when I got really focused on remaking myself for that park pitch, and I stayed in that fired-up, really confident headspace for… yeah, around two weeks before I sort of crashed. I don’t know if that’s the kind of length you mean, but that’s my best estimate.
After that fired-up period ended, did you go through a stretch where you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?

Yeah… yeah, I did.

I mean, I try not to make it sound too dramatic, but it’s been kind of hanging over me for, honestly, about a year now. And after that fired-up stretch ended, this latest crash has been… probably the worst it’s gotten.

So yes, most days it’s been there. I don’t know if I’m explaining that right.
During that fired-up time, did you believe you had special powers, a special mission, or abilities far beyond what was realistically possible for you?

Not special powers, no… I don’t think I thought anything like that. Not like supernatural or anything.

But I did kind of believe I had this… I don’t know, bigger ability or calling with the landscaping stuff than was probably realistic. Like I honestly thought I was about to become the person every town around here would call for sustainable landscaping, even though in real life I’m still just trying to keep my small jobs paid up.

Saying it that way sounds kind of ridiculous, but at the time it felt completely possible. Does that answer what you mean?
At any time when you were not in that fired-up state, did you still have unusual beliefs that other people said were clearly not true?

I don’t think so… not that I’m aware of.

I mean, I’ve had worries or ideas that other people maybe thought were too much, but when I’m not in that fired-up state, I don’t think I’m holding onto anything that people are telling me is clearly not true. At least… nobody’s really said that to me.

Is that the kind of thing you mean?
During that fired-up period, did your behavior ever get so severe that you were hospitalized or taken to the emergency room because of it?

No… I don’t think it ever got to that point.

Like, nobody took me to the ER or anything, and I wasn’t hospitalized for it. It was definitely not my finest time, but as far as that specific thing, no. Is that what you’re asking?
